newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's biggest travel agency cancels Peru trips.
newsitem.headline: Japan's biggest travel agency cancels Peru trips.

text.p: Japan's biggest travel agency said on Wednesday all five tours to Peru it planned for the Christmas holiday period had been cancelled because of the week-long hostage crisis.

"We have cancelled all five due to a prolonged unpredictable situation in Peru," a spokeswoman for the Japan Travel Bureau (JTB) told Reuters. "We got a few inquiries (about safety) and decided to cancel the trips altogether before we got too many of them."
Peru has become a popular destination for free-spending Japanese tourists in the six years since Peruvian-Japanese President Alberto Fujimori came to power.
Nearly 10,000 Japanese tourists visited Peru in 1995.

But the cancellation of the Christmas tours appeared to be an early sign that the still unresolved rebel takeover of the Japanese ambassador's residence could cause Peru to fall from favour as a holiday destination.
However, not all travel agents advised Japanese tourists to avoid Peru.
"We are proceeding with our tours. We have confirmation that there are no inconveniences concerning travel and sightseeing in the area," a spokesman for Kinki Nippon Tourist said.
He said one 20-member group left for Peru on Tuesday.
"A tour to Peru does not mean to Lima. The main attractions are the ruins, especially those in Cuzco and Machu Picchu. Lima is only a stop-over point," the spokesman said.
While the JTB spokeswoman said the travel agency had not yet decided whether to proceed with tours scheduled for January and beyond, its competitor had no plans to halt its operations in Peru.
"For Japanese people, a trip to Latin America is something exotic. Most people who decide to go have already travelled extensively around the world," the spokesman for Kinki Nippon Tourist said.
"For them, Latin America is an attractive option and this means that those who sign up have a strong will to go."
